subject: Culture
title: Holi and Social Inversion
description: A fast breakdown of Holi and Social Inversion for builders.

hook.text: During Holi, people throw colored powder at strangers. For one day, caste and class dissolve.

buildup.text: Holi marks the triumph of good over evil, rooted in the legend of Prahlad and the demon Holika.

discovery.text: The festival's chaos is the point. Norms break so society can reset. Anthropologists call it social inversion.

twist.text: Holi celebrations have now spread to secular 'color runs' worldwide. The ritual lost its religion.

climax.text: Festivals that briefly erase hierarchy reveal what societies secretly want: equality, even for a day.

punchline.text: Color hides every difference for one afternoon.

quiz.question: What concept do anthropologists use to describe Holi's erasure of social hierarchy?
